findings.description: Dwell-history trim uses a fixed ${DWELL_HISTORY}.tmp path with > redirection rather than mktemp or explicit symlink rejection, so a pre-created symlink could redirect root-owned writes.
If tail fails, the cleanup removes DWELL_HISTORY but not ${DWELL_HISTORY}.tmp, so a transient tail failure leaves a stale temp file in /run that can accumulate.
run_case writes an empty argument with printf '%s\n', creating one blank line instead of a zero-byte file, so T1's empty-history case never exercises the empty path.
T9's outer DWELL_HISTORY assignment uses the test shell's PID while the inner bash -c reassigns it with its own $$, so the child path is not what cleanup() removes and the test passes vacuously.
